proposed.text: Trap #38 addresses contrast percentage requirements in BP 344 for two different elements: tactile strips and stair nosings. What are the correct percentages for each?

options.text: Tactile strips: 30% luminance contrast; stair nosings: 50% luminance contrast
Tactile strips: 50% luminance contrast; stair nosings: 30% luminance contrast
Tactile strips: 50% luminance contrast; stair nosings: 50% luminance contrast — same requirement for both
Tactile strips: 70% luminance contrast; stair nosings: 30% luminance contrast — tactile strips require higher contrast

rationale.summary: Trap #38: tactile strips = 50% luminance contrast; stair nosings = 30% luminance contrast.
rationale.explanation: Trap #38 in the article. BP 344 specifies two different luminance contrast percentages for two different elements: tactile floor/wall surfaces require 50% luminance contrast with adjacent surfaces; stair nosings require only 30% luminance contrast. The trap is easy to construct on an exam by swapping the two percentages. Tactile strips need higher contrast because they must be visible from a standing or walking approach; stair nosings are already at foot level and require only moderate contrast.
common_misconceptions: Applying the same percentage to both elements — they have different contrast requirements (50% vs. 30%)
Selecting 70% for tactile strips as 'even safer' — 50% is the specified standard, not 70%

proposed.explanation: Two contrast standards: tactile strips = 50%; stair nosings = 30%. A common exam trap swaps these two values.
